title: My Forever Portfolio: 4 Spectacular Stocks You Can Buy Now and Never Sell
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Parkevtate sets out his forever-portfolio framework: over very long horizons competitive advantages matter more and valuation less, though valuation still counts. First is Eli Lilly (LLY), a pharma company with decades of R&D successes, the weight-loss franchise being only the latest; he owns it and wants to add more, and its stated price and DCF fair value were garbled in the captions (prior DCF $1,523 on 20 October). Second is Visa (V), whose two-sided network of over 4 billion cards is nearly impossible to replicate: merchants must accept it, and from his own experience selling his book online, Visa's ~39c plus 3% fee is such a tiny share of operating costs that even halving it would not justify switching. Its market price is $423 with the fair value garbled in captions. Third is Coca-Cola (KO), a century-old brand whose global distribution, marketing and sales network took decades to build; it recently won KFC away from PepsiCo, and he values it at $100 against a $96 price near its 52-week high. Fourth is Colgate-Palmolive (CL), a first tracked call, with a similarly capital-intensive, hard-to-replicate manufacturing and distribution moat in a slow, saturated industry with shrinking shelf space; it trades at $97 against a DCF fair value above $120. He cautions that buy-and-hold-forever still requires monitoring the moats. Calls: LLY BUY, V BUY, KO BUY, CL BUY — all reiterated except CL, which is new.
